name: Insulator Creek Falls
description:
RSVP accepted via this platform - ❌

RSVP via email to walk leader directly - ✅👍

Please Note: Selecting Going on Facebook Events does not automatically register you for this event. Please contact the leader directly at info@veteducation.com.au (Cherry Judge) to secure your spot on this TBWC hike. This is important due diligence for our club insurance. 

Who is leading - Cherry Judge

This coming Sunday, 1 February, we’re heading out to Insulator Creek at Bambaroo.

Meeting time: 6:30 am  [location will be emailed by Saturday]

When will we return - we will aim to return by 3 pm 

About

Rated – Medium Hard.Terrain – Bush tracks, uneven footings (tree roots, rocks), steep climb (all climbing on the track for 3-4 hours on way up), with some off-track creek walking around midday (steep track descent/ascent, bushbashing, exposed ledges, rockhopping, slippery rocks, wet shoes likely). 

We don’t often get to do this walk in conditions like this, but after the recent rains it’s going to be beautiful. Fig Tree Falls should be flowing well, and Insulator Creek Falls will be full too, which makes this a pretty special time to be out there.

The big attraction for me though are the giant fig trees. They are a sight to behold!

Definitely one of those walks that really comes into its own after rain.

If you’re keen for a stunning post-rain walk and a good day out with the club, hope you can join us.

What to Bring - http://tiny.cc/whattobring

RSVP  - to Cherry Judge directly via email - info@veteducation.com.au

Club Members - free

Club visitors are welcome - it is $5 to cover our club insurance.

You can do 3 walks and qualify to become a TBWC member!

See you on the adventure,

Cherry

name: Wallaman Off Track
description:
Townsville Bushwalking Club Walk
Wallaman Falls - Butterfly Falls Lookout and Hearts Falls.
Saturday 21 February 5am
Distance: ~6km
Duration: Half day
Grade: 3-4 off-track
Terrain: Open bushland, light scrub, minor undulations
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

We are heading back up to the Wallaman Falls area for a short, exploratory half-day wander through open bushland.

We will leave Townsville at 5:00 am sharp on Saturday 21 February and carpool up to the Wallaman Falls camping ground. From there, we will head off-track through relatively open forest, making our way toward Butterfly Falls Lookout and then on to a small peak with views across to Hearts Falls - staying outside the restricted zone at all times.

This is not the tourist track version of Wallaman. Expect a mostly flat walk through open woodland with sections of light scrub and minor angulations. The terrain is generally forgiving, but there will be uneven ground, loose leaf litter and the usual North Queensland surprises underfoot. Good navigation, situational awareness and long sleeves are recommended.

Distance will be modest and the pace steady. This is intended as a short half-day walk, with time to explore lookouts, enjoy views across the Herbert River Valley and return to the campground before late morning heat builds.

Bring:
At least 1.5-2 L of water
Morning tea
Hat and sun protection
Long sleeves and pants
Sturdy footwear
First Aid Kit and PLB

Wallaman Falls is Australia’s tallest single-drop waterfall at 268 m, but this walk is about the broader landscape - the dry open forest, escarpment edges and those dramatic side-on views into the gorge system that most visitors never see.

RSVP details will be circulated to the group. Early start, cooler air, and a quiet escarpment before the crowds arrive - that is the plan.

name: Diorite Falls - Paluma
description:
Townsville Bushwalking Club Walk
Diorite Falls - Paluma Range National Park
Sunday 22 February
Walk leader: Cherry
Grade: 4
Distance: 15-22 km depending on route
Duration: 6-8 hours
Terrain: Forest trails, creek crossings, rock hopping, moderate undulations

To RSVP, please email info@veteducation.com.au

Cherry will be leading us to Diorite Falls, a beautiful 10 m slab waterfall on Waterfall Creek in Paluma Range National Park. Named after the igneous rock "diorite" found in the area, this is one of those classic Paluma destinations - granite slabs, clear pools and lush creek lines tucked into the forest.

This will be a solid day walk. Depending on the route taken and group pace, expect between 15 and 22 km and around 6 to 8 hours on foot. Difficulty is Grade 4 - moderate to difficult - with a mix of trail walking, off-track sections and creek navigation.

There are a couple of possible approaches. We may cross the Paluma Dam wall and head north-east through the forest, or enter Waterfall Creek from the northern track and rock hop upstream to the falls. Final route choice will depend on conditions and group ability on the day.

The reward is well worth it. Diorite Falls spills smoothly over a broad slab into a large inviting pool - ideal for a lunch stop and, for those keen, a refreshing swim. Just be mindful that wet season creek edges can harbour leeches, and slippery rock demands careful foot placement.

Cherry will organise any required permissions for the day.

Bring:
At least 2-3 L of water
Lunch and snacks
Swimmers and small towel
Sturdy footwear suitable for wet rock
Long sleeves and pants
Gaiters optional but useful in creek sections

This is a longer day in Paluma’s cool upland forest, with a proper waterfall payoff at the end. Expect a steady pace, good company and the kind of granite-and-water scenery that makes North Queensland special.
